The Sun will end up the size of Earth

text:
What creates the colors in Jupiter's clouds?

No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium, elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops.

Source: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, "Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno" (22 Nov 2026).
https://science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2026-november-22-swirls-and-colors-on-jupiter-from-juno/
replies:
Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research, although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate. What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image – and many similar images – is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones.

Image: NASA, Juno, SwRI, MSSS; Processing & License: Matt Brealey, Seán Doran.
